a.raw: mrs rachel lynde walked through avonlea every morning
a.why: Capital letters on the title and names (Mrs. Rachel Lynde), a capital on the place name (Avonlea), a period at the end. Common nouns like "morning" stay lowercase.

b.raw: the brook ran past mrs rachels door in lyndes hollow
b.fixed: The brook ran past Mrs. Rachel’s door in Lynde’s Hollow.
b.why: Capital at the start of the sentence, capitals on the title and names, apostrophes to show the door belongs to Mrs. Rachel and the hollow to the Lyndes, and a period at the end.

scholar.journal-q1: … and name one thing the narrator tells you about Matthew that Mrs. Rachel does not know.
scholar.journal-q2: … and for each detail, say what it makes you feel about living in Avonlea.
scholar.journal-q3: … and quote the line that shows it most clearly.

fill1.h1: The word means to join things together. Which of the two prefixes is spelled with an n?
fill1.why: con- means "with" or "together," so connect is to join one thing together with another.

fill2.h1: Say it out loud: com-bine. Listen to the letter just before the b.
fill2.why: com- means "together." To combine is to bring things together into one.

fill3.h1: A company is a group of people together. It takes the same prefix as combine.
fill3.why: com- means "together," so company is the people who go along together.

fill4.h1: To continue is to keep going with what you started. Same prefix as connect.
fill4.why: con- means "with," so continue is to keep going with the thing you began.

match.placid: Placid is about calm, not about company.
match.imagine: Imagining happens in your head — look for the meaning about pictures in the mind.
match.companion: A companion is a person, so its meaning should describe a person.
match.delight: Delight is a feeling. Look for the meaning that names a feeling.

sort.child → children: Children does not end in -s at all — the whole middle of the word changed.
sort.woman → women: Listen to the vowel: woman, women. The change is inside the word, not on the end.
sort.foot → feet: No ending was added here — oo simply became ee.
sort.road → roads: Roads is the ordinary -s rule, nothing surprising.
sort.gable → gables: Gables just adds -s. Nothing inside the word moved.
sort.window → windows: Windows adds -s like most nouns do.
sort.cats: Cat takes a plain -s — nothing hisses at the end.
sort.boxes: Try saying "boxs." The x makes you need the extra -es.
sort.brushes: Try saying "brushs." The sh makes you need the extra -es.
sort.stories: Story ends in consonant + y, so the y became an i before -es.

connector: Last week you closed Mrs. Frisby and stood it on your shelf. Today we open a new one. Anne of Green Gables begins quietly — a woman at her window, a man driving past in his good suit, and a question she cannot leave alone. Watch how much Montgomery tells you about Avonlea before anybody in it says a word.
